title: Whisper: Robust Speech Recognition at Scale
hook: Train a plain encoder-decoder transformer on 680,000 hours of weakly-labeled multilingual audio and you get near-human transcription robustness without task-specific fine-tuning.
key_points: A standard encoder-decoder transformer trained on ~680k hours of diverse web audio - no custom acoustic model needed.
Weak supervision from naturally occurring audio-transcript pairs scales data collection without expensive human labeling.
Handles transcription, translation to English, language ID, and timestamps in a single multitask model.
Open weights across multiple model sizes (tiny to large) enable local deployment without API access.
content_html: Radford and colleagues at OpenAI published Whisper in December 2022, demonstrating that scale and diversity of training data can substitute for elaborate domain-specific speech recognition engineering. By scraping roughly 680,000 hours of audio with associated transcripts from the web, they trained a model that generalizes robustly to accents, noise conditions, and languages that typical ASR systems struggle with.
extra_html:
How it works

Audio is converted to log-mel spectrograms and processed by a convolutional stem before entering a standard transformer encoder. A transformer decoder then generates text tokens autoregressively, conditioned on the encoded audio. The model is trained on a mix of tasks specified by special tokens: transcribe in the original language, translate to English, detect the language, or predict timestamps. This multitask framing is handled in one model without task-specific heads.

Why it matters

Whisper showed that general-purpose sequence modeling and large-scale weak supervision can reach near-human accuracy in speech recognition across many languages, eliminating the need for hand-engineered acoustic features or careful domain adaptation. Its open weights made high-quality transcription accessible for local use cases, and its architecture has since been integrated into products like GPT-4o. Explore the paper and model weights on arXiv.

related.hook: Translate a sentence by reading it into one vector, then writing a new sentence out of that vector. This encoder–decoder recipe powered early neural machine translation.
